transcript.text: And what are your choices if someone

or they shoot you.
>> Wrong. You take the gun, or you pull out

or you do any one of 146 other things.
There's two types of problem solving in
life. There's convergent, which is what
they teach you at school. There's lots
of variables and there's one correct
answer. And there's divergent thinking,
which is that there's many correct
answers to a single problem. Most of
life is divergent solutions, not
convergent solutions. So, for example,
if I said, "How many uses of a brick can
you think of?" Somebody who has a
convergent process would only say, "Uh
bricks only build buildings." But
somebody who has a divergent thinking
process would think, "Okay, well I could
use it as a doorstop. I could use it as
a paperweight. I could spray paint it
gold and make it a trophy. I could drill
holes into it and use it as a potted
plant some dirt inside of it. I could
use it for a pathway to walk on."
There's so many different uses of a
brick, but the people who struggle in
life only see one way out and they see
it as a brick wall in front of them.
